The Art of Understated Elegance at Masseria Moroseta

August 12, 2026

The Planning
The Inspiration
This wedding editorial, curated and designed by Manda of Mae&Co Creation at Masseria Moroseta, was inspired by the desire to create something both aesthetically refined and deeply connected to the atmosphere of Puglia itself. Every detail was designed to feel effortless while honoring the architecture, textures and slower rhythm of Southern Italy. Known for its clean lines, whitewashed walls and sculptural minimalism, Masseria Moroseta became the foundation of the entire visual direction. Rather then competing with the venue, the design was created to enhance it through soft blue florals, refined tablescapes and crystal lighting elements that echoed the clarity and geometry of the space. The result feels modern yet deeply romantic, a contemporary interpretation of destination wedding elegance rooted in the quiet beauty of Puglia.
The Venue
Masseria Moroseta offered the perfect setting for this editorial through its balance of minimal architecture, natural beauty and quiet luxury. Surrounded by olive groves and Mediterranean light, the venue already carries such a naturally editorial atmosphere, balancing rural simplicity with refined modern design. As a working agricultural estate producing its own olive oil and embracing a true farm-to-table philosophy, the Masseria invites couples into a slower and more intentional rhythm of celebration. Weddings here become multi-day experiences centered around connection, presence and Italian slow living, where guests gather not only for the wedding itself, but to share meals sourced directly from the land, explore the surrounding countryside and immerse themselves in the culture of Puglia and nearby Ostuni. Beyond the Masseria, the experience extends to the sea. From the nearby port of Gallipoli, restored 1990s Italian motorboats offer private Mediterranean day trips and intimate coastal cruises, adding another layer of nostalgia and effortless Italian romance to the destination wedding experience.
Beauty
Flat Lays
The Fashion
Wedding Gown
The bridal styling centered around two distinct Eva Lendel gowns, each reflecting a different emotional tone of the celebration while maintaining the same refined and fashion-forward sensibility. The ceremony look featured a dramatic sculptural ballgown with an off-the-shoulder neckline and architectural folds that framed the body almost like couture drapery. The silhouette felt modern yet timeless... soft in movement, but visually commanding. Against the minimal white walls of Masseria Moroseta, the gown became almost architectural itself, creating striking monochromatic moments throughout the editorial. The clean fabric, exaggerated proportions and sweeping train brought a sense of effortless grandeur without feeling overly traditional. For the evening, the styling shifted into something more sensual and luminous with a fully embellished off-the-shoulder Eva Lendel gown. Covered in delicate shimmering beadwork, the second look captured the transition from golden hour into candlelit celebration beautifully. The sheer sleeves and subtle sparkle introduced a glamorous old-Hollywood feeling while still remaining understated and refined. Together, the gowns created a complete bridal narrative that mirrored the progression of the day... from sculptural daytime elegance to intimate evening glamour... while remaining cohesive through the styling, palette and modern Italian setting.
Bridal Portraits
Fashion
The Details
Florals &amp; Decor
The floral and decor direction focused on creating an atmosphere that felt organic, sculptural and deeply connected to the venue itself. Every element was approached with intention, balancing softness and refinement while allowing the natural beauty of the Masseria to remain central. Large hydrangea clusters, delicate delphinium and cascading orchids were paired with stoneware vessels, textured linens and organic produce to create an earthy yet elevated tablescape. The pastel palette softened the modernity of the venue in a way that felt romantic without ever overwhelming the architecture. Vintage-inspired Italian garden chairs, crystal glassware and freestanding chandeliers introduced a more editorial layer to the reception design while still maintaining intimacy and warmth. As the light shifted throughout the day, the atmosphere transformed with it... airy and minimal beneath the afternoon sun, then moodier and cinematic as evening approached. The overall design was intended to feel immersive, emotionally soft and visually timeless... a modern interpretation of Mediterranean destination wedding styling grounded in the textures and landscape of Puglia.
Tips To Pull Off The Look
To achieve a bridal aesthetic like this, the focus should remain on balance and intentionality. Every styling choice was designed to feel elevated without competing for attention. The beauty direction stayed clean and refined throughout both looks, featuring luminous skin, softly sculpted makeup and a sleek infinity-inspired updo that created continuity across the editorial. The result felt polished yet effortless, modern without appearing overly styled. For the ceremony gown, the emphasis was placed on shape, movement and architectural simplicity. Minimal accessories and restrained styling allowed the sculptural silhouette to fully speak for itself against the clean surroundings of the Masseria. The evening look introduced a more sensual energy through delicate embellishment, subtle shimmer and softer evening light. While the atmosphere became moodier and more glamorous, the styling still maintained the same sense of restraint and sophistication established earlier in the day. Ultimately, what tied both bridal looks together was the focus on timeless fashion over trends. From the tailored silhouettes to the understated beauty choices, every detail was designed to feel contemporary, editorial and emotionally wearable for the modern destination bride.
